title: Bleeding Edge Alert! Sparse Linear Methods (SLIM)

cues.en: It's time for another bleeding edge alert.
cues.zh: 又到了前沿研究提醒。

cues.en: This is where we talk about some recent research that has promising results but hasn't yet made it into the mainstream with recommender systems yet.
cues.zh: 這裡介紹近期一些有潛力、但尚未成為推薦系統主流的研究。

cues.en: In this bleeding edge alert, we're actually going back to the year 2011 to look at sparse linear methods, or SLIM for short.
cues.zh: 這次其實要回到 2011 年，看看稀疏線性方法，簡稱 SLIM。

cues.en: This came out of the University of Minnesota, which has been a pioneer in the field of recommender systems from the very beginning.
cues.zh: 它來自明尼蘇達大學，這所學校從一開始，就是推薦系統領域的先驅。

cues.en: The results from SLIM were very exciting and I don't know why we don't hear about it being used in industry more.
cues.zh: SLIM 結果很令人興奮，我不知道為什麼沒更常聽到業界使用。

cues.en: It's something definitely worth watching and keeping an ear out for.
cues.zh: 絕對值得持續關注。

cues.en: What caught my attention with this paper is how consistently SLIM outperformed a wide variety of competing algorithms on a wide variety of data sets.
cues.zh: 這篇論文吸引我的，是 SLIM 在各式各樣資料集上，都能穩定勝過許多競爭演算法。

cues.en: Although they didn't include SVD++ in their comparisons, but they did compare against many similar algorithms.
cues.zh: 雖然比較沒有包含 SVD++，但確實比較了許多類似演算法。

cues.en: Also, they measured their success on hit rate, so their focus is very much on top-end recommendations instead of rating prediction accuracy, which again is the right thing to focus on.
cues.zh: 而且，它們以命中率衡量成功，因此聚焦的是 Top-N 推薦，而不是評分預測準確程度，這再次是正確方向。

cues.en: But not only did SLIM beat the pants off of everything else on the Netflix data set, it also wins with data sets from a bookstore, from Yahoo Music, from credit card purchasing data,
cues.zh: SLIM 不只在 Netflix 資料集大勝其他方法，也在書店、Yahoo Music、信用卡購買資料，

cues.en: and a couple of mail-order retailer data sets as well.
cues.zh: 以及幾個郵購零售商資料集上勝出。

cues.en: The only data set where it didn't come out on top was, ironically, MovieLens, but it placed a close second.
cues.zh: 諷刺的是，唯一沒拿第一的資料集是 MovieLens，不過也只差一點，排名第二。

cues.en: The idea behind SLIM is to generate recommendation scores for a given user and item by a sparse aggregation of the other things that user has rated, multiplied by a sparse aggregation of weights,
cues.zh: SLIM 的概念是，透過稀疏地彙整使用者評分過的其他項目，再乘上稀疏的權重彙整，產生某位使用者對某個項目的推薦分數，

cues.en: which is where the magic lives.
cues.zh: 而神奇之處就在權重。

cues.en: Here's what the notation in the paper looks like.
cues.zh: 這是論文中的符號。

cues.en: Tilda a sub ij represents the unknown score for a given user for a given item, and that's equal to the entire row of stuff that the user has rated, here indicated by a sub i T
cues.zh: ã_ij 代表某位使用者對某個項目的未知分數，等於這位使用者評分過項目的整列資料，這裡用 a_iᵀ 表示，

cues.en: multiplied by some precomputed weights associated with that row.
cues.zh: 乘上與這一列相關、預先計算的權重。

cues.en: Because the user has only rated some items, and weights only exist for these items, that's where the word sparse comes from in this method.
cues.zh: 因為使用者只評分過部分項目，權重也只存在於這些項目，所以方法名稱裡有「稀疏」。

cues.en: So if you extend this idea to the entire user item rating matrix, it looks like this.
cues.zh: 把概念擴展到整個使用者－項目評分矩陣，就像這樣。

cues.en: Pretty simple, right?
cues.zh: 很簡單，對吧？

cues.en: To predict ratings, we just multiply the rating we know about by some magical weight matrix called W.
cues.zh: 預測評分，只要把已知評分，乘上一個叫做 W 的神奇權重矩陣。

cues.en: Both A and W are sparse matrices, meaning it contains incomplete data, just the ratings that actually exist.
cues.zh: A 與 W 都是稀疏矩陣，也就是資料不完整，只包含實際存在的評分。

cues.en: So the secret sauce is in how W is computed, and this is where it gets complicated, so complicated that a lot of people have trouble implementing it, which might explain why it's not more widely used.
cues.zh: 祕訣在於如何計算 W，而這裡變得很複雜，複雜到很多人難以實作，可能解釋了為什麼沒有更廣泛使用。

cues.en: This is just the first couple of paragraphs from the paper that describes how to do it.
cues.zh: 這只是論文中，描述做法的前幾段。

cues.en: At its heart, it's an optimization problem just like we used to cast a gradient descent to learn the matrices in SVD.
cues.zh: 核心是最佳化問題，就像之前使用隨機梯度下降，學習 SVD 的矩陣。

cues.en: But you seriously need a higher degree in mathematics to understand what's going on here.
cues.zh: 但真的需要高階數學學位，才能理解這裡發生什麼事。

cues.en: If phrases like matrix Frobenius norm and L1 norm regularization make sense to you, then knock yourself out.
cues.zh: 如果矩陣 Frobenius 範數、L1 範數正規化這些詞，你都懂，那就盡情研究。

cues.en: But otherwise, I'll be snooping around on GitHub for people who have already implemented this successfully and shared their code for it.
cues.zh: 否則，我會在 GitHub 找找，有沒有人已成功實作，並分享程式碼。

cues.en: I did find one, but the guy who wrote it had trouble getting it to work at scale.
cues.zh: 我確實找到一個，但作者在擴展到大規模時遇到困難。

cues.en: It's not easy stuff at all.
cues.zh: 這完全不簡單。

cues.en: Still, you can't argue with SLIM's results.
cues.zh: 不過，SLIM 的結果無可否認。

cues.en: So if you see it offered as part of a machine learning library you're working with, it's definitely worth your time to experiment with it.
cues.zh: 因此，如果所用的機器學習函式庫提供它，絕對值得花時間實驗。

cues.en: The research community has taken note, and some extensions on SLIM have emerged, such as contextual SLIM and higher-order SLIM, or HOSLIM.
cues.zh: 研究社群也注意到了，出現一些 SLIM 擴充，例如情境式 SLIM，以及高階 SLIM，簡稱 HOSLIM。

cues.en: Even in the original paper, an extension called fsSLIM, or feature-selection SLIM, is described, which restricts SLIM to use only use columns most similar to what you want.
cues.zh: 原始論文中甚至描述了 fsSLIM，也就是特徵選擇 SLIM，限制只使用與目標最相似的欄。

cues.en: This improves hit rate ever so slightly.
cues.zh: 這會讓命中率稍微提升。

cues.en: So if a SLIM implementation comes your way, give it a second look.
cues.zh: 因此，如果遇到 SLIM 實作，值得多看一眼。

cues.en: It's promising stuff.
cues.zh: 它很有潛力。
